content.content:
#### Description

The tab is one scrolling column, with a [ScrollbarScope](../../scrollbar/index.md#scrollbar-scope), read top to bottom as a timeline, in three groups, each headed by a small muted label with its count: "Previous", every task that has run, oldest at the top, as the [PromptEditor](../../../../scope/prompt-mode/index.md#prompt-editor)'s previous tasks are, with their filters and batch actions along the group's heading; "Running", every task under way, in either lane; and "Queued", the queue, in its order, as the [QueueListScope](../../../../scope/prompt-mode/queue-list/index.md#queue-list-scope) says, reordered by dragging, its auto-send switch and "Send next" button along its heading. A group with nothing in it shows its heading alone, muted, "No queued prompts" and the like. Each time the tab is shown, it is scrolled so the Running group, or the start of the Queued one when nothing runs, is in view.
The Previous group starts collapsed: its heading alone shows, with its count and a right chevron, and none of its rows. Clicking the heading, anywhere but its filter and batch actions, expands it, the chevron turning down, its rows showing above Running, the newest nearest it, and clicking again collapses it. It is collapsed each time a project is opened, and otherwise stays as it was left while the application runs, each open project keeping its own. While it is collapsed, its filters and batch actions still work and its count still follows them, and opening a previous task from elsewhere, as from the running activity list, expands it to show that task.

#### Rows

Every task is one row, 28 pixels tall, as a queued prompt's is: a bar 2 pixels wide down its left edge in its mode's colour, as the [PromptModesScope](../../../../scope/prompt-mode/modes/index.md#prompt-modes-scope) colours it, then its status, a spinner while it is under way, a tick, cross, or dash once it has ended, or, queued, its place in the queue, then the first line of its prompt, cut off with an ellipsis, then, at its right, muted, how long it took, or has been running, as the [MessageList](../../../../scope/prompt-mode/message-list/index.md#message-list) writes it. A chain is one row, its steps as rows indented beneath it, collapsed to start with, as the previous tasks group a chain. Clicking a row opens it, as below, and the row stays highlighted while it is open. Hovering a row shows its prompt's first lines in its tooltip.

#### Virtualized

The list is virtualized: however many tasks the project has run, it lays out and draws only the rows in view, and a few rows either side of it, never every row, so opening the tab, scrolling it, resizing the sidebar, filtering, and new tasks arriving cost the same with ten thousand previous tasks as with ten. Every row is 28 pixels tall, group headings and a chain's expanded steps included, so where each row lies is known from its place in the list alone, without laying out the rows before it, and the scrollbar's thumb is sized and placed from the whole list's height, as though every row were drawn.
A row is drawn only from what its row shows, its mode, status, first line, and time, read from each task's history record once and kept, never by reading a record's output, lines, or snapshots while scrolling; those are read only when a task is opened. Running rows update their time and spinner in place, redrawing only what is in view. Scrolling to a row, as when the tab opens on Running, a filter changes, or a queued row is dragged past the edge, jumps straight to its place without drawing the rows between. A row scrolled out of view and back is the same as it was, its chain expanded or not, its selection and highlight kept.
Scrolling past either end does nothing: with the list at its top or its bottom, a wheel, trackpad, or drag that goes further leaves every row exactly where it is, frame after frame, with no stretch, bounce, or nudge of even a pixel and back, and draws nothing anew, since nothing moved. Its scroll position is clamped to its ends before a frame is drawn, never drawn past an end and corrected the frame after, and kept in whole device pixels, so a row never shimmers between two places. What lies at an end stays at it: a running row's time ticking, a task finishing, a row added or removed elsewhere in the list, or the tab being resized never makes the rows in view jump and settle. A list scrolled to its bottom stays at its bottom as rows are added, and one at its top stays at its top. The list counts as taller than the tab only once it overflows it by a whole pixel, as the right sidebar's panels do, so a list that fits never scrolls at all.

#### Details

        The three groups are accordion sections, each collapsible on its
        own. A section's heading is a row 28 pixels tall, on the theme's
        raised surface, a step apart from the rows: a chevron at its left,
        pointing right while collapsed and down while expanded, then its
        title and count, then, at its right, its own controls, Previous's
        filter and batch actions and Queued's auto-send switch and "Send
        next". Clicking the heading, anywhere but its controls, expands or
        collapses that section alone; any number can be expanded at once,
        and collapsing one takes its rows away and leaves only its heading.
        Previous starts collapsed and Running and Queued expanded, each time
        a project is opened; otherwise each stays as it was left while the
        application runs, each open project keeping its own. A collapsed
        section still counts its tasks, its controls still work, and opening
        one of its tasks from elsewhere, as from the running activity list,
        expands it to show that task.

        Each heading is sticky: while its section's rows are scrolled
        through, the heading stays pinned at the top of the tab, over the
        rows scrolling beneath it, until the next section's heading reaches
        it and pushes it up and out of view, the next one taking its place.
        So the heading of the section in view is always showing, with its
        count and controls in reach, however far down it is scrolled. A
        pinned heading draws over the rows with its own surface, never
        letting them show through, and is drawn once, never twice where it
        is pinned and where it lies.

EOF

content.text:
The Tasks tab is now three collapsible accordion sections with sticky headings, every row lines up in the same columns, and chains no longer expand inline. `piton check` reports no problems and `piton build` wrote 82 files.

- **Accordion sections:** Previous, Running and Queued each collapse on their own.
  - Each heading is a 28px raised row: a chevron, the title and count, then its controls at the right.
  - Clicking a heading toggles only that section, and any number can be open at once.
  - Previous starts collapsed and the other two expanded whenever a project opens. Otherwise each project keeps them as you left them.
- **Sticky headings:** a section's heading stays pinned at the top while you scroll its rows, until the next section's heading pushes it out. Pinned headings never let rows show through and never move any row.
- **Aligned columns:** every row in every section uses the same columns:
  - the mode bar;
  - a 20px lead column: a checkbox in Previous, a drag grip in Queued, kept empty in Running;
  - a 20px status column;
  - the prompt;
  - a right-aligned time.

  So status and text start at the same place whatever the row has, and the headings' titles line up with the rows' text.
- **Chains:** a chain is one row with its overall status and its step count. Its steps show only once you open it, and selecting the row selects its steps for batch actions.

**Anchors the code should follow:** `TasksTabScope` `#description`, `#rows`, `#virtualized` and `#chain-steps`, and `PromptEditor` `#chained-tasks`.
